text:
maya: heads up — after last night's BIOS sweep in eu-west-2 we started seeing a handful of nodes drop out of provisioning during PXE. seems related to BMC reboots and NIC firmware mismatch
jasper: saw alerts from the fleet watcher too. some nodes came back with SecureBoot state toggled to 'disabled' which blocked our signed PXE loader
srinivas: can you paste one of the BMC logs? curious if iDRAC/iLO rolled to a fallback image during the flash
maya: logging from host-gpu-47: `BMC: Firmware upgrade applied, rebooting. UEFI varstore crc mismatch -> SecureBoot=0; PXE: link up, but tftp 404 for signed-boot.efi`
ana: infra-bot posted the batch job summary: `bios-sweep-job-2026-03-17: 12/480 failed, 5 transient, 7 requiring manual intervention`
jasper: 12/480 is ok but the 7 manual ones are all in the same rack (rack-eu-west-2c). could be a NIC firmware revision skewing PXE driver. want a quick gate to stop the rest of the rollouts?
maya: please stop rollouts. i've paused the pipeline for all eu-west-2. if we leave it going we'll risk more nodes flipping secureboot and failing provisioning
srinivas: agree. i'm going to run a quick NIC firmware inventory and cross-check model/rev with the BIOS delta. command i used: `fleetctl hwscan --filter "region:eu-west-2" --fields mac,model,nic_fw`
liam: FYI cost note — if we hold capacity and keep OC pods running we will start incurring ~3.2k/day in reservation bleed for Dedicated clusters in the region. should be fine short-term but worth flagging to infra-finance
jasper: noted. let's target a mitigation path: 1) rollback BIOS on the 7 affected nodes 2) reflash NIC firmware if rev mismatch 3) re-enable SecureBoot with signed shim 4) run a canary of 10 nodes in another rack
maya: rollback plan looks good. can someone run the rollback and coordinate maintenance window? i'll file a ticket and mark affected nodes: host-gpu-41..host-gpu-48 (rack-eu-west-2c)
srinivas: starting rollback now. using `oobctl flash --target host-gpu-4{1..48} --image bios-2026-01-18.bin --verify` and will watch infra-bot for status.
infra-bot: rollback started for hosts: host-gpu-41,host-gpu-42,host-gpu-43,host-gpu-44,host-gpu-45,host-gpu-46,host-gpu-47,host-gpu-48
jasper: after rollback, we should force a SecureBoot enable sequence and verify varstore. snippet to run on each node: ```bash
ssh oob@<bmc>
ipmitool sel elist
curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/uefi/enable-secureboot
reboot
```
maya: reminder: the enable-secureboot endpoint will refuse if the varstore CRC doesn't match. run `uefi-tool --repair-varstore` first if the CRC check fails
liam: also pinging compute-ops to see if we can temporarily divert new provisioning to us-east-1 while this stabilizes — minimizes impact to dev teams and keeps SLAs intact
ana: update from rollback: infra-bot shows host-gpu-41..44 succeeded, 45..48 in progress; one node (host-gpu-47) reported `NIC FW mismatch: expected 3.1.2 got 2.9.0` and auto-flash failed due to locked bootbank
srinivas: for bootbank lock we'll need physical intervention or out-of-band vendor tool. i've opened a hardware-service ticket and flagged high priority. vendor ETA ~6 hours
jasper: ok. we should proceed with canary on other racks that are known-good. maya can you pick the 10 nodes and i'll trigger a controlled provision
maya: picking canary nodes now: host-gpu-101..110 (rack-eu-west-2a). triggering canary provision in 15m
liam: thanks — finance OK'd the short reservation hit until we restore full capacity
ana: infra-bot: canary provision started for host-gpu-101..110; expected time ~22m
jasper: if canary passes, we can resume BIOS sweep with an added NIC-fw precheck and strict varstore checksum validation. add a soft-fail stop on first two manual nodes
maya: logging the postmortem draft in #postmortems after we stabilise. immediate actions: pause rollout, rollback 7 nodes, vendor intervention for locked bootbank, canary in 2 racks, resume with prechecks
srinivas: i'll follow up here when vendor confirms physical intervention scheduled
liam: ping me if this extends past EOD so i can loop in execs on SLA risk/cost
maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
